objective: Implement v0.3.3 as a real npx-managed DSH Crew lifecycle CLI with first-class install, status, update, and uninstall commands, including stable Crew-owned package persistence so installations never depend on a transient npx cache path.
context: Issue #48 is the product specification. Public UX must be `npx @ran-sh/dsh-crew@latest install|status|update|uninstall`. Current source setup supports install/status/uninstall only and assumes a source checkout with pnpm/dev build; a packaged npx path must instead consume the already-built npm payload and persist the runnable Crew package under Crew-owned state before Harness registration. Keep source-checkout setup compatibility. The Crew Harness authority/isolation remains ~/.config/dsh-crew/harness with profile dsh-crew. Never inspect or mutate normal ~/.dsh, official web profile, OpenCode auth stores, or credential values. This task is implementation + validation only; v0.3.3 publication/tag/Release is not authorized.
forbidden_changes: git tag creation, deletion, or movement
credentials, tokens, OTPs, auth headers, credential-store contents, or npmrc contents
normal ~/.dsh or official DSH web profile
OpenCode auth.json or other provider credential stores
weakening or rewriting user pnpm/npm security policy such as minimumReleaseAge
validation: Run targeted setup/install/distribution/CLI tests, adding focused tests for the new bin and lifecycle semantics.

Run a real local-tarball npx lifecycle in a fully disposable HOME/USERPROFILE: pack the candidate, invoke the package through npx/npm exec from outside the repository, then install -> status -> update -> status -> uninstall -> status. No step may touch the normal user Crew/DSH state.

During the disposable npx lifecycle, prove the Harness registration target and runnable installed package live under the disposable Crew-owned state, not the repository checkout, tarball path, temp extraction path, or npm/npx cache. Remove all task-created tarball/extraction inputs after install and prove status/DSH registration still works from the persisted payload.

Exercise same-version update idempotence and a test-owned repair case by making a bounded disposable Crew-managed registration/payload state stale or incomplete, then prove `update` repairs it without deleting config/credentials and without destroying the prior usable install before replacement validation succeeds.
Run a source-checkout compatibility lifecycle or equivalent high-signal source setup tests proving `node scripts/setup.mjs install|status|uninstall` remains supported.

npm pack --dry-run --json and verify package name/version 0.3.3, the executable bin is included, required runtime/setup payload is included, and tests/agent-results/ACTIVE_TASK/secrets/temp artifacts are excluded.
acceptance_criteria: package.json exposes exactly one natural CLI executable for the package so `npx @ran-sh/dsh-crew@latest <command>` resolves without requiring an explicit binary name; install, status, update, and uninstall are supported and unknown commands fail with useful usage text/nonzero exit.

package.json, src/runtime-identity.mjs, and CHANGELOG.md identify candidate version 0.3.3; README.md and README.zh.md make npx the primary install/manage UX while retaining source-install documentation as a developer/alternative path.

npx install/update never require a source checkout, pnpm lockfile, devDependencies, or rebuilding lib/client.js; they use the published prebuilt package and establish a durable Crew-owned installed payload before registering it with Harness.

The durable installed payload path is under Crew-owned state and remains usable after the invoking npx package/cache/tarball input is unavailable; Harness registration never points to an ephemeral npx/npm cache or task temp path.
status is read-only and reports candidate CLI version plus installed Crew version when determinable, DSH plugin state, Codex integration state, and Claude integration state.

update is upgrade-aware, preserves Crew config and all credentials, validates/stages the candidate before switching, repairs registration/integrations, is idempotent when current, and does not remove the last working install before the replacement is ready.

uninstall removes the Crew-managed installed package payload plus Crew plugin registration and host integrations while preserving normal Crew config/backups by default; existing --purge behavior remains explicit and destructive only when requested.
Windows real disposable npx lifecycle passes; macOS/Linux path and process behavior has deterministic automated coverage. No normal user state or official DSH/provider credentials are accessed.
Full deterministic tests, build, normal npm install verifier, official DSH cohort verifier, pack audit, and publish dry-run all pass with no uncommitted generated artifact left behind.

Result Contract status is PASS only if the real disposable npx lifecycle and all required deterministic/package gates pass; include final_machine_state describing the normal machine and confirm no publication/tag/Release occurred.
